rationale: 的 written for the degree-complement marker 得 (画得很细致 -> 画的很细致). v6 de_particle keeps only 得/地 confusion and missing 得 (corruption rule §1.4: '得 removed, 得→地, 地→得'); 的-for-得 is listed as contested (frequent in casual native writing) and C11 bars contested forms from positives. The DT gold README also already lists '得/的 variant' as acceptable variation for clean items, so the current label contradicts the gold set's own convention. Strict jev reading (C11) would exclude the item from hard negatives too; for DT purposes the reproduction is acceptable, so the item becomes a clean/variant_ok item.

corrected_form: 我的朋友们都夸我的T恤很可爱
rationale: Attributive 的 written as adverbial 地 before a noun (我地朋友们). Unlike 的-for-地, this direction is not on any 'Not an error' list and a textbook copy editor would correct it in standard written Mandarin. It is still a 的/地/得 structural-particle confusion, so de_particle is the right lesson. CAVEAT: v6 de_particle's wording ('before a complement or adverbial, or an obligatory 得 missing') does not literally cover the attributive slot, and §1.4's edit list omits 的→地; orthography (accuracy/minor) is the only other candidate and bands are identical either way. Also note 我地 is Cantonese written form for 我们 (V5 dialect reading), but the passage is Mandarin, so it is not rescued.
cited_rule: merged_taxonomy.json zh.de_particle definition (G, accuracy, minor); taxonomy.md §0.8 rule 2 (textbook-correction test) and rule 4 (type fit)

rationale: 私たちは作るものは: 私たち is the subject of the relative clause [私たちが作る]もの, which is itself the main-clause topic (…ものは). A reading '私たちは、作るものは…' (contrastive/double topic) is strained without a comma and was not the source's structure. The register error (マジ) is unaffected.

context.reference: The coding is important. You write instructions for the Arduino. You can make the arm pick up small things. You can move them to a new spot.
context.reproduction: The coding is important. You write instructions for the Arduino. You can make the arm pick up small things. You can move it to a new spot.

learner_form: move it to a new spot
corrected_form: move them to a new spot
severity_change: none (major retained; note v6 word_choice default_severity is minor)
rationale: them->it. Not a case error, reflexive-binding error, which-for-person or resumptive pronoun, so it falls outside v6 pronoun. It is also not ungrammatical standalone: 'it' has a plausible antecedent ('the arm'), so 'You can move it to a new spot' is well-formed (§0.8 rule 5 would reject it as a grammar positive). What changed is meaning: the learner now moves the arm, not the objects. That is a fidelity defect; word_choice (wrong lexical choice, fidelity) is the closest v6 home. Severity kept major (the propositional content changes) although word_choice's default is minor. agreement is subject-verb only; plural_number is noun morphology — neither fits.
cited_rule: merged_taxonomy.json en.pronoun definition (case / local reflexive / which-for-person / resumptive) and en.word_choice definition; taxonomy.md §0.8 rules 4 and 5

context.reproduction: The coding is important. You write instructions for the Arduino. You can make the arm pick up small things. You can move him to a new spot.

learner_form: You can move him to a new spot.
corrected_form: You can move them to a new spot.
rationale: them->him with no male/person antecedent in the passage. Not a case error, reflexive, which-for-person or resumptive pronoun, so outside v6 pronoun. It is a wrong lexical pronoun (number + animacy/gender) that breaks the link to 'small things' — a fidelity/meaning defect, closest v6 home word_choice. Not semantic_anomaly: moving 'him' is not an impossible event, just an unanchored referent. Severity major retained. Reviewer note: jev's en.B3 bucket question mentions pronouns 'referring to the right person', which a reviewer could read as supporting 'keep'; the type definition itself is narrower, so I retype.
cited_rule: merged_taxonomy.json en.pronoun (narrow binding scope) and en.word_choice; taxonomy.md §3.2 en.pronoun type details; §0.8 rule 4
